- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with recent low range.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply upward bias of 2–4% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.0 → 0.25 → 0.33), model often fails to anticipate sharp upturns; add 1–2% buffer to forecast.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment spikes, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price reaction.
